note: Conversations now look like the photo: a large portrait of the person you are talking to stands on the left with their name plate beneath it, and a wide text box below carries what they say, with the game still visible behind the panel. Every villager has a face — ten characters with six expressions each — and the face changes with the conversation: they smile at compliments and warm friendships, glare when insulted or cold toward you, look sad at bad news or a joke that falls flat, talk while they speak, and turn to profile when showing their wares. And what they say is now real: rumors come only from gossip they actually heard or things that actually happened to them — no more invented secrets — and a villager with a quest for you will mention it by name. Everything from before still works: topics that deepen, haggling, disposition prices, and merchant shops in conversation.
